header.title: Programming Paradigms and Languages
header.lead: These courses help students understand that programming is not only syntax. It is a way of modeling problems, organizing computation, and selecting a style of reasoning suited to the task.

data.text: This family groups courses and tutorials in functional programming, logic programming, object-oriented programming, Python programming, Java, and advanced language practice. The aim is to help students see the strengths and limits of different paradigms rather than treating each language as an isolated technical island.

data.text: The learning sequence usually starts from familiar imperative examples and then introduces alternative ways of expressing the same problem. Students compare styles, rewrite solutions, and discuss the consequences for readability, modularity, reuse, and correctness.

items: [b]Comparative exercises[/b]: the same problem may be solved with different paradigms to reveal trade-offs.
[b]Code reading[/b]: students learn to infer design intent from existing code.
[b]Mini-projects[/b]: object-oriented or Python/Java projects help connect language constructs with application structure.
